root.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Allgaier, Schlechter Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. h4 g4 5. Ng5 Nf6

overview: In the Allgaier after 3.Nf3 g5 4.h4 g4 5.Ng5, White has given the f-pawn and is ready to sacrifice the knight on f7. With 5...Nf6 (the Schlechter defence) Black develops and leaves the knight on g5 attacked; White follows with Bc4 or d4 and a fierce fight with Black extra pawns. It is highly theoretical and double-edged.

white_ideas.idea: Attack f7 with Ng5 and Bc4
Sacrifice Nxf7 when it opens the king

black_ideas.idea: Hold the pawns and block with ...h6

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on g4 and f4, advanced

character.notes: Sharp tactical chaos with kings exposed.

gambit.notes: Black has the f4 and g4 pawns and can keep material with accurate defence.

approach.notes: Rarely played by strong players now.

level.notes: Long forcing lines that must be known.

character.reason: Mutual attacks with exposed kings, where one error loses.

gambit.reason: White has given the f-pawn and offers more.

soundness.reason: Theory thinks Black can hold the material, and White is the side taking the risk.

structure.reason: Open lines and files drive the play.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Allgaier now.

level.reason: Long forcing theory has to be known.

plans.reason: White throws pieces at f7 and the king.
